title: Matsya brings back the Vedas
word: the ten avatars as a series
hook: the Vedas slip from sleeping Brahma, and the fish dives after them
carry: the vedas are heard, and handed on by mouth
tomorrow: the gods need a mountain to churn the sea. who holds it up?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the ten avatars as a series: Matsya's boat through pralaya, where an age ends and the seeds and sages go on, with a neighbor's ark beside it. Today the fish dives once more, after the stolen Vedas, and the week looks back.

Some things you only notice are missing when you reach for them: a charger, a key, a grandmother's recipe. In the Bhagavata Purana's telling, an age is ending, and Brahma, the creator, drifts into sleep. The Vedas slip from his mouth. A demon has been waiting for exactly that. He snatches the sacred words and dives with them into the deep. And the fish goes in after him.
screen: `MISSING WHEN YOU REACH FOR IT.` → `THE VEDAS SLIP FROM BRAHMA.` → `THE FISH DIVES.`

segments.voice: The demon's name here is Hayagriva. That name came up this week as the horse-headed Vishnu who teaches Agastya; in this story it belongs to someone else, a thief. Matsya finds him in the deep, defeats him, and brings the Vedas back, so when Brahma wakes and the world begins again, the sacred words are there. Why would God dive for words? In Hindu teaching the Vedas are shruti, what was heard. Many Hindus hold that no person wrote them; sages heard them, and they've been handed on by mouth, teacher to student, ever since. Seeds, sages, and now the Veda: the fish keeps what's needed to begin again. Now the week, one card at a time. Lalita rose from the gods' fire with a sugarcane bow, and desire was given its place back, inside dharma. Her hymn called her name after name, and saying the name was the prayer. The Adhyatma Ramayana kept the real Sita safe in the fire: many Ramayanas, and Sita never Ravana's. A row of avatars, one Vishnu coming down. A fingertip fish that turned out to be the Lord. A boat through the end of an age, with a neighbor's ark beside it. And now the sacred words, carried up out of the deep.
screen: `THE THIEF IS CALLED HAYAGRIVA.` · `MATSYA BRINGS THE VEDAS BACK.` · `SHRUTI: WHAT WAS HEARD.` · then, large: `HANDED ON BY MOUTH.`

segments.voice: If you know a mantra, say it once, softly, the way it was taught to you, mouth to ear. Then close your eyes and hear it again in the voice of whoever taught it. If you don't pray, let a line come back that someone older once handed you, and stay with it for the sit.
The ten avatars as a series: Matsya, the first descent, brings the Vedas back up from the deep.

fork.setup: a classmate asks why Vedic chanting is still taught by ear, teacher to student, when every word is printed. by Matsya's dive?

fork.reveal: Matsya dove so the Vedas wouldn't be lost when the world began again. they're shruti, what was heard, and they're still handed on by mouth.
